A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIPPER and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. The framework and retained experiments can be matched despite extensive restructuring.

before.justification: v1 Section 4 and the appendices report original experiments on MATH, GSM8K, and MMLU-STEM, including prompt diversity, aggregation, and self-reflection results.

after.justification: v2 Section 5 and Appendix C report original experiments, including retained reasoning benchmarks and additional model, BIG-Bench, and prompt-diversity evaluations.

M1.justification: The prompt generator, fidelity-adjusted semantic-volume selection, and majority voting remain. The optional aggregation procedure changes from an LLM synthesizing constituent responses to Best-of-N selection using an external reward model. The rewritten selection objective is algebraically equivalent to v1's objective.

E1.justification: MATH, GSM8K, and MMLU-STEM are retained. v2 Appendix C.3 adds BIG-Bench synonyms, word unscrambling, and word sorting, extending evaluation beyond the original mathematical and STEM reasoning coverage.

E2.justification: The main Self-ensemble, Random+, and Top-n comparator set is retained after renaming. The separate MV-versus-LLMA comparison in v1 Table 1 disappears. v2 Figure 8 instead compares FASV with Self-ensemble under Best-of-N; it does not display the other variants discussed in the accompanying text.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaMA3.2-3B, Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B, and Llama3.1-8B configurations, Best-of-N evaluation with Qwen2.5-Math-RM-72B, and instruction induction from five input-output demonstrations. It also introduces a candidate-pool control using k-means with k=4. The original benchmark splits and 4/8/5-shot settings remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds clustered-versus-full candidate-pool analysis, GSM8K diversity sensitivity and scatter analyses, and a paraphrased-versus-diverse prompt case study. It removes the MV/LLMA override-ratio and unique-answer diagnostics. Self-reflection evidence is narrowed from an ensemble-size sweep to a single n=5 comparison.

E5.justification: The retained self-reflection result loses its displayed spread: v1 Figure 4 includes a shaded band, whereas v2 Section 5.5 reports only the n=5 accuracies. Neither version defines that band or specifies repeated-run counts or seeds. Other error-bar and shaded-spread displays remain.

E6.justification: v2 adds LLaMA, Qwen3, and BIG-Bench results and removes v1's MV/LLMA table. Retained curves also change: GSM8K Random+ at n=3 moves from approximately 84.10 to 83.73 (v1 Figure 7; v2 Figure 12), and MMLU-STEM scores are revised. The MATH correlation plot changes substantially, with its peak moving from about 0.41 to 0.82 (Figure 6 in both versions).

T1.justification: v2 Equation 7 and Appendix B add an explicit derivation decomposing fidelity-adjusted semantic volume into log-determinant diversity plus alpha times total prompt fidelity. This derivation is absent from v1, although the underlying objective and existing submodularity-based argument are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claim of training-free, prompt-diverse ensembles built from one base LLM, including three Qwen2-MATH-1.5B instances outperforming a 7B model. The new contribution bullets organize existing claims; additional experiments mainly extend their support.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the fidelity-diversity interpretation, explaining why excessive fidelity weighting can hurt and why candidate-pool diversity matters. It adds an easier-task explanation for limited GSM8K gains, discusses applicability beyond reasoning, and explicitly acknowledges the homogeneous-model limitation. The earlier explanation of LLMA's reasoning-based advantage is removed.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A newly identifies all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and specifies temperature 0.7, top-p 0.8, repetition penalty 1.05, and a 512-token generation limit. It also identifies the Best-of-N reward model. These disclosures do not establish changed settings for retained experiments. The detailed LLMA prompt template is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated prompt-optimization discussion distinguishing single-prompt search from ensemble composition, citing works including Zhou, Lin, Yang, and Hu. It also newly connects prompt selection to data-selection research and the diversity objective to determinantal point processes, substantially broadening v1's mainly ensemble-focused positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, contribution bullets are introduced, and problem formulation becomes a separate section. Prompt-generator material moves from the appendix into the main method description, while the experimental narrative and appendices are reorganized. Author order and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with substantially rearranged and resized figures. The algorithm and prompt-accuracy distribution move into the main text. New model, diversity-analysis, and BIG-Bench displays are added; the LLMA comparison table and self-reflection plot are removed.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support relies principally on one specialized constituent model. v2 substantially strengthens generality through additional model families and non-reasoning tasks, adds controlled analysis of candidate diversity, and improves reproducibility through encoder and decoding details. The explicit objective derivation also aids understanding. Lost LLMA diagnostics and reduced self-reflection reporting are drawbacks, and Table 5 contains exceptions to the claimed consistent superiority, but the broader and more examinable evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
